A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 50-page versions of KAN: Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks. Pages 2–50, including Appendices A–F, have identical extracted text and rendered appearance. Page 1 differs only in publication-status and arXiv metadata.

before.justification: v4 reports original experiments on function fitting, PDE solving, continual learning, knot theory, and Anderson localization, plus LAN experiments and hyperparameter analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains the same original empirical results in Sections 3–4 and the appendices, including function-fitting comparisons, scientific-discovery examples, and LAN experiments.

M1.justification: The spline-based KAN architecture, grid extension, sparsification, pruning, and symbolic-function procedures in Section 2 are unchanged. Appendix B retains the same LAN architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic, special-function, Feynman, PDE, continual-learning, knot-theory, and Anderson-localization tasks. Appendix B also retains the same image-fitting experiment.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout, including the MLP activation variants in Section 3.3 and the SIREN/MLP comparisons with LANs in Appendix B.

E3.justification: The training and evaluation settings are identical, including the Feynman architecture and grid sweeps in Section 3.3 and the LAN image-fitting schedule in Appendix B.3. No metrics, sample sizes, or testing procedures change.

E4.justification: Appendix B retains the analysis separating learnable activations from their placement on edges. Appendix C retains the same sensitivity analyses for entropy regularization, seeds, penalty strength, grid size, and spline order.

E5.justification: Seed information and statistical reporting are unchanged. For example, Section 3.3 still specifies three random seeds per hyperparameter combination and selection of the best models across seeds and depths.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted curves, rankings, and qualitative findings are identical, including the Feynman results in Table 2 and Appendix D and the LAN results in Appendix B.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Theorem 2.1, its assumptions and proof, and the approximation and scaling-law reasoning in Section 2 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and concluding discussion retain the same claims about accuracy, interpretability, scaling, and scientific discovery. Their scope remains focused on demonstrated small-scale AI + Science tasks.

C2.justification: Section 6 retains the same mathematical, efficiency, and applicability limitations. Appendix E retains the same tentative explanation and unresolved concern about performance degradation at large grid sizes.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, training instructions, and code-access information are unchanged. Appendix A retains the same API descriptions, and embedded link destinations match.

R1.justification: Section 5, the bibliography, and the positioning relative to earlier Kolmogorov–Arnold, spline, learnable-activation, and symbolic-regression research are identical.

P1.justification: Page 1 replaces 'Preprint. Under review.' with 'Accepted by International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR) 2025.' The arXiv version/date also changes. The remaining prose, terminology, and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: All figures, tables, captions, placements, and pagination are unchanged, including the image-based appendix results. The revised first-page metadata occupies the existing layout.

improvement.justification: v5 updates publication-status and arXiv metadata while retaining the same scientific content, evidence, limitations, reproducibility information, and presentation structure. The acceptance statement alone does not establish an improvement in paper quality; the PDFs show no meaningful net quality difference.
